habits: Build a small home lab (an old laptop or free virtual machines is enough) and write up what you try.
Do beginner capture-the-flag challenges and keep a simple public portfolio of what you learned.
Go to a local ISSA, ISACA, OWASP or BSides meeting. Most are free for students, and many jobs come from people you meet there.

roles.name: SOC Analyst
roles.tagline: The organization's lookout: you watch for signs of trouble and raise the alarm.
roles.summary: A Security Operations Center (SOC) analyst watches alerts from an organization's computers and networks, decides which ones are real problems, and passes serious ones to responders. It is the most common first job in cybersecurity.
day: Review a queue of alerts and decide which are false alarms and which need action
Look up a suspicious email, website or file to see whether it is harmful
Write short notes so the next shift knows what happened
roles.feeder: IT help desk or support roles are the usual way in, but many SOCs hire graduates directly.
steps: Learn the basics of networks and operating systems (CompTIA Network+ material is a good map).
Practise reading alerts on free blue-team labs.
Earn one starter certification, then apply to SOC, security operations and managed security provider jobs.

resources.name: TryHackMe
resources.note: Free beginner rooms, including SOC basics

resources.name: LetsDefend
resources.note: Practise working a SOC alert queue

resources.name: Blue Team Labs Online
resources.note: Free defensive challenges

items: Watching for anything unusual on a team's screens and raising the alarm
Working on a team that keeps watch over an organization day and night
Sorting through lots of alerts to find the few that are real problems

roles.name: Incident Responder
roles.tagline: The emergency team: when an attack gets through, you contain it and clean up.
roles.summary: Incident responders take over when an attack is confirmed. They stop it from spreading, remove the attacker, get systems back to normal and explain what happened to leaders.
day: Join a call when a ransomware alert fires and decide what to shut off first
Collect evidence from affected computers before it is lost
Write the after-action report and recommend fixes
roles.feeder: Most responders spend 1 to 3 years as a SOC analyst first.
steps: Start as a SOC analyst and volunteer for incident work.
Learn how attacks unfold, step by step, using MITRE ATT&CK.
Practise on free investigation challenges.

resources.name: CyberDefenders
resources.note: Free investigation challenges

resources.name: NIST SP 800-61
resources.note: The standard US guide to incident response

resources.name: MITRE ATT&CK
resources.note: How real attackers operate, step by step

items: Being the person called in when something goes badly wrong
Leading a calm cleanup after a cyberattack
Staying calm and making quick decisions when everyone else is stressed

roles.name: Digital Forensics and Cybercrime Investigator
roles.tagline: The detective: you recover digital evidence and work out exactly what happened.
roles.summary: Forensic investigators recover and examine data from computers, phones and online accounts, then explain what it shows in a way that holds up with managers, lawyers or a court. Jobs exist in police labs, government, consulting firms and legal services.
day: Make an exact copy of a phone or laptop without changing the original
Rebuild a timeline of what a user or attacker did
Write a report a lawyer or judge can follow
roles.feeder: Some police labs, e-discovery firms and consultancies hire graduates as forensic technicians; others want SOC or IT experience first.
steps: Learn how files, operating systems and phones store data.
Practise with free forensics tools and challenges.
Look for forensic technician, e-discovery and law enforcement civilian analyst postings.

resources.name: Autopsy
resources.note: Free, open-source forensics tool

resources.name: CyberDefenders
resources.note: Free forensics challenges

resources.name: NIST SP 800-86
resources.note: Guide to adding forensics to incident response

items: Recovering deleted files to find out what really happened
Helping police or lawyers build a case from evidence on a phone or computer
Piecing together a timeline from small clues, like a detective

roles.name: Threat Intelligence Analyst
roles.tagline: The researcher: you study attackers so the organization can see them coming.
roles.summary: Threat intelligence analysts research criminal and state-backed hacking groups: who they target, how they operate and what they are likely to do next. They turn that research into briefings and warnings that help defenders prepare.
day: Read reports, news and hacker forums for signs of new attacks
Match a group's methods to known techniques
Brief leaders on which threats matter most to the organization
roles.feeder: Most start as SOC analysts, or as intelligence analysts in government or the military.
steps: Read public threat reports and summarize them in your own words.
Learn MITRE ATT&CK, the shared language for attacker behaviour.
Strong writing matters as much as technical skill, so practise it.

resources.name: MITRE ATT&CK
resources.note: Catalogue of real attacker groups and techniques

resources.name: SANS Institute on YouTube
resources.note: Free talks, including threat intelligence summits

resources.note: How analysts move between roles

items: Researching a criminal hacking group and writing up how it operates
Following world news to predict who might attack next and why
Turning reports and news into a short briefing for leaders

roles.name: Penetration Tester
roles.tagline: The ethical hacker: you break in, with permission, so the real attackers can't.
roles.summary: Penetration testers are hired to attack an organization's systems with permission, find weaknesses before criminals do, and explain how to fix them. It is a popular goal, but few people are hired into it straight from school.
day: Scan a client's network for weak spots agreed in advance
Try to get from an ordinary account to full control
Write a report that ranks what to fix first
roles.feeder: Common first jobs are vulnerability management analyst, systems administrator or SOC analyst.
steps: Learn networking and Linux first; most testing builds on them.
Do capture-the-flag challenges and write up each one.
Look for vulnerability management or junior security analyst jobs while you build skills.

Solving puzzle-style hacking challenges for fun

roles.name: Application Security Engineer
roles.tagline: The builder-defender: you make sure software is safe before it ships.
roles.summary: Application security (AppSec) engineers help developers write safe code. They review designs and code, run security tests and fix or explain the weaknesses they find.
day: Review a new feature's code for mistakes attackers could use
Set up automated security checks that run on every code change
Teach developers how to avoid a common mistake
roles.feeder: Most move in after time as a software developer.
steps: Learn one programming language well and build something real.
Study the OWASP Top 10, the most common web app weaknesses.
Practise finding bugs in deliberately broken apps.
certsStart: A portfolio of code and write-ups matters more than certificates here

resources.note: The most common web app risks

resources.note: Free hands-on labs

items: Writing code and making sure it can't be misused
Reviewing an app before launch to catch mistakes that could let attackers in
Building websites or apps with security designed in from the start

roles.name: Cloud Security Engineer
roles.tagline: The cloud guardian: you keep services on AWS, Azure and Google Cloud locked down.
roles.summary: Cloud security engineers design and check the security of systems that run on cloud platforms such as Amazon Web Services, Microsoft Azure and Google Cloud. Much of the work is setting things up correctly and automating checks.
day: Find a storage bucket that was accidentally left open to the internet
Write rules that stop risky settings from being deployed
Decide who should have access to which systems
roles.feeder: Usually reached from cloud, systems administration or developer roles.
steps: Start with one cloud provider's free beginner training.
Build a small project in the cloud and lock it down.
Learn basic scripting (Python or Bash) for automation.

items: Setting up online services on Amazon, Microsoft or Google cloud
Automating how computer systems are built and locked down
Working with the online services that apps and websites run on

roles.name: GRC Analyst
roles.tagline: The planner: you set the rules and priorities that keep a business safe.
roles.summary: Governance, risk and compliance (GRC) analysts help an organization decide which risks matter, write the policies everyone follows, and show regulators and customers that security is under control. It suits people who like structure, writing and working with business teams.
day: Update a security policy after a new law or contract requirement
Run a risk assessment with a business team
Gather evidence for an upcoming audit
roles.feeder: Often hired straight from business, IS or accounting programs.
steps: Learn one framework well, such as the NIST Cybersecurity Framework.
Practise writing a short policy or risk register for a made-up company.
Apply to GRC, risk, compliance and security analyst roles.

Deciding which risks matter most to a business and what to fix first
Turning complicated rules into clear checklists people can follow

close.note: GRC and IT audit are close cousins. GRC builds and runs the security program from the inside; IT audit checks it, often from outside, and grades it.

roles.name: IT Auditor
roles.tagline: The independent checker: you test whether an organization really does what it says.
roles.summary: IT auditors test whether an organization's technology controls actually work, then report what they find to leaders, boards or regulators. Large accounting firms and internal audit departments hire many graduates each year.
day: Interview a team about how they grant and remove system access
Test a sample of records to see whether the rule was followed
Write findings with a clear rating and recommendation
roles.feeder: Commonly hired straight from accounting, business or IS programs, especially by large accounting firms.
steps: Take an auditing or internal controls course if your program offers one.
Join ISACA as a student; chapters often run student nights with employers.
Apply to IT audit, technology risk and internal audit graduate programs.
certsStart: ISACA student membership (not a certification, but a good first step)
certsLater: ISACA CISA (you can sit the exam early; the certificate needs 5 years' experience, partly waivable)

Visiting different organizations to review how they protect themselves and write a report card
Testing whether a process really works by checking samples of real records

roles.name: Privacy Analyst
roles.tagline: The data rights advocate: you make sure personal information is handled fairly and legally.
roles.summary: Privacy analysts make sure an organization collects, uses and shares personal information legally and fairly. They interpret privacy laws, review new products and handle requests from people who want to see or delete their data.
day: Review a new app feature for what personal data it collects
Answer a customer's request to see the data held about them
Explain a new state privacy law to a product team
roles.feeder: Some graduates are hired directly; others come from GRC, legal or compliance roles.
steps: Learn the basics of US state privacy laws and Europe's GDPR.
Read companies' privacy policies critically and note what they reveal.
Look for privacy analyst, privacy operations and compliance analyst roles.

Reading privacy laws and explaining what a company has to change
Speaking up for people whose personal information is being collected

roles.name: Security Awareness Specialist
roles.tagline: The teacher: you help people spot scams and make safer choices.
roles.summary: Most attacks start with a person: a scam email, a fake phone call, a reused password. Security awareness specialists design training, simulated phishing and campaigns that change how people behave, and measure whether it works.
day: Run a simulated phishing email and review who clicked
Make a short video or game about spotting scam calls
Present to new employees about protecting their accounts
roles.feeder: Often reached from training, communications, education or help desk roles.
steps: Learn how common scams work: phishing, smishing and voice phishing.
Create a sample training piece for your portfolio.
Apply to security awareness, human risk and security training roles.

resources.note: Guide to building a security learning program

resources.name: SANS Security Awareness resources
resources.note: Free reports and planning materials

items: Teaching people how to spot scam emails, texts and calls
Making videos, games or posters that help people stay safe online
Explaining tech risks to people in plain, friendly language

roles.name: Network and Systems Security Administrator
roles.tagline: The keeper of the systems: you run networks and servers and keep them secure.
roles.summary: Network and systems administrators keep an organization's computers, servers, accounts and networks running, updated and secure. It is one of the most common doors into cybersecurity, and the skills carry into almost every other role.
day: Install security updates across hundreds of computers
Set up accounts and permissions for a new employee
Fix a network problem stopping an office from working
roles.feeder: IT support and help desk are the usual first jobs; many graduates start here directly.
steps: Learn networking basics and practise in a free network simulator.
Get comfortable with the Linux and Windows command line.
Apply to IT support, systems administrator and network technician roles.
certsLater: CompTIA Security+, then a specialist certification

resources.note: Free network simulator

resources.name: OverTheWire Bandit
resources.note: A free game that teaches the Linux command line

items: Setting up computers, networks and user accounts so everything runs smoothly
Fixing computer problems and keeping systems up to date
Setting up computers and home networks just to see how they work

roles.name: OT / ICS Security Specialist
roles.tagline: The infrastructure protector: you secure power, water and factory systems.
roles.summary: Operational technology (OT) and industrial control systems (ICS) run power grids, water treatment, pipelines and factories. Specialists here protect equipment where a cyberattack can cause physical harm, so safety and reliability come first.
day: Map which plant machines are connected to which networks
Plan a security update that cannot interrupt production
Work with engineers to separate safety systems from office networks
roles.feeder: Often reached from controls engineering, field technician or IT and security roles in utilities and manufacturing.
steps: Learn how industrial systems differ from office IT.
Take CISA's free industrial control systems training.
Look at utilities, manufacturers and engineering firms, which often train new hires.

resources.note: Free online industrial security courses

items: Protecting power plants, water systems or factories
Working with real machines and equipment, not just office computers
Finding out how factories, power grids or vehicles are controlled by computers

roles.name: AI Security Specialist
roles.tagline: The new frontier: you find ways AI systems can be tricked and help make them safer.
nice: No single NICE work role yet; draws on Vulnerability Analysis and Secure Software Development
roles.summary: AI security specialists test and protect AI systems such as chatbots and machine learning models: tricking them into misbehaving, stopping data leaks and defending against attacks that target the models themselves. The field is new, so few entry-level postings exist yet.
day: Try to trick a company's chatbot into revealing private data
Review how an AI feature handles untrusted input
Write guidance for teams building with AI
roles.feeder: Usually reached from AppSec, machine learning engineering, data science or SOC roles.
steps: Learn how AI language models work at a basic level.
Play free prompt-injection games and write up what worked.
Build a security foundation first; most AI security work rests on it.
certsStart: No widely recognized entry certification yet; focus on projects
